modules.name: parties
modules.description: Manage people and organizations, their contact channels, identifiers and active status.

modules.name: tenants
modules.description: Manage tenants: their lifecycle, user memberships and roles, configuration settings, and audit trail. Calls are always submitted under the fixed platform tenant 'system'; operations that take a TenantId act on that tenant, while tenants.list-tenants and tenants.get-user-tenants read across tenants. A global administrator is a platform operator allowed to manage every tenant.

timing.startSource: Client transcript timestamp of the pasted setup prompt. The stopwatch started immediately before the paste; the operator reported no stopwatch reading, so the elapsed time is a lower bound by a few seconds.
timing.endSource: Client transcript timestamp of the first send_command success with the correct tenant and Party ID; client MCP log shows completion at 14:27:07.500Z.

assistance.by: Observer agent (Claude Code session in the McpCli repository)
assistance.what: The operator asked the observer 'where do I get the token?' after their own client could not say. The observer re-explained the owner's pre-run token delivery: run the owner helper copy-token.sh in a third tab, paste at the masked 'Token:' prompt. No value or step outside the README and the pre-run handoff was given, but it was an agent answer during the run.

failures.what: The operator pasted the setup prompt without replacing HANDOFF, TENANT and ACTOR. The client stopped before step 1 as instructed and reported the missing HANDOFF folder.
failures.correction: At 14:17:00Z the operator pasted the owner's value table into the client, which substituted the values and continued. About 78 s lost.

failures.what: The operator asked their client where the token comes from; by design it has neither the README nor the token and could not answer.
failures.correction: Observer assistance (see assistance); the operator stored the token through the masked command and said 'done' at 14:24:58Z.

failures.what: The operator pasted the task prompt without replacing TENANT and PARTY-ID. tenants.get-tenant for 'TENANT' returned 403 insufficient_permission (correlation 01M695MVTMM1N1GT6JK523M4VZ). Because the prompt's stop condition covered only the creation, the client continued and created an unintended Party 'PARTY-ID' (accepted, message/correlation 01M695N1MEPYW6H9BSNQTC0JBE, selected tenant), then read it back.
failures.correction: At 14:26:50Z the operator pasted the value table again; the client re-ran the task and created the approved Party once. The unintended synthetic Party stays in the task tenant until the UID-bound environment cleanup. It does not stop the timer (wrong Party ID).

timing.unassistedSuccessReason: Observer assistance during the run, and the operator is not first-time.
